narrative.intro: Mission Support and Test Services reports $953M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date, from four awards with an average award size of $238M. The Department of Energy is the dominant buyer, accounting for the full $953M in obligations for the period. Obligations fell 4.2% year over year, following a peak of $1.1B in FY24 and a $995M total in FY25. Facilities Support Services is the primary market, matching the $953M in obligations tied to the Department of Energy. Smaller activity appears in General Automotive Repair, with $61.2K obligated through the General Services Administration. The vendor’s current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity. Historical obligations show multi-year volatility, with totals of $855M in FY21, $923M in FY22, $838M in FY23, $1.1B in FY24, and $995M in FY25. The concentration of FY2026 obligations in one agency and one market suggests a narrow revenue base for the fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: Who are the main buyers of Mission Support and Test Services?
sections.body: The Department of Energy is the main buyer, obligating $953M in FY2026 to date. The General Services Administration also bought services, with $61.2K in obligations. The buyer list shows a strong concentration in one agency for the current fiscal year to date. That concentration links directly to the Facilities Support Services market activity.

sections.heading: How have obligations trended over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Obligations rose to $1.1B in FY24 and then fell to $995M in FY25, before registering $953M in FY26 to date. Obligations were $855M in FY21, $923M in FY22, and $838M in FY23. Year-over-year change for the current period is down 4.2%. The path shows variability across the five-year span.

faq.q: How much does Mission Support and Test Services make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Mission Support and Test Services has $953M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The vendor has four awards this fiscal year to date with an average award size of $238M, and total obligations for the period are down 4.2% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Mission Support and Test Services?
faq.a: The Department of Energy and the General Services Administration buy from Mission Support and Test Services. The Department of Energy obligated $953M in FY2026 to date, and the General Services Administration obligated $61.2K.

faq.q: What does Mission Support and Test Services sell to the government?
faq.a: Mission Support and Test Services sells Facilities Support Services and General Automotive Repair to the government. Facilities Support Services accounts for $953M in obligations and General Automotive Repair accounts for $61.2K.
